evidence.source: 裘錫圭, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.field: 甲骨文、金文及楚簡的字形释读
evidence.text: 裘錫圭 distinguishes Shang oracle-bone graphs with a seated person below 目 as 見 and a standing person as 視, arguing from their different inscription contexts and the distinct 視/見 forms in the Guodian Chu slips. He rejects the earlier proposal that the standing-person form was a variant of 望. He also identifies Western Zhou bronze forms with a standing person as 視, while noting that an early phonetic spelling using 見 and 氏 coexisted with the pictographic form. These are the scholar’s paleographic conclusions, not an uncontested reading of every individual graph.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：甲骨文中的見與視

evidence.source: 裘錫圭, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The article cites oracle-bone contexts such as 視師 and 視方 and argues that the first means observing an enemy force in preparation for battle. It also discusses Western Zhou bronze inscriptions including 墻盤 and 伯簋, interpreting their graph as 視. The article was originally published in 1999; it reports Shang oracle-bone and Western Zhou bronze evidence, but the inspected text does not assign an absolute date to any one oracle-bone token.
evidence.title: 裘錫圭：甲骨文中的見與視

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: The entry records the received Shuowen wording 瞻也。从見、示 and Duan Yucai’s reading 从見，示聲. It says 視 is filed under 見 because 見 is its primary semantic element in the received form. This supports the traditional analysis of 見 as semantic and 示 as phonetic for this compound form, while not establishing that the earliest graph had that structure.
evidence.title: [A03769] 視 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry lists senses including looking, examining or observing, treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating, and a use glossed as 通「示」. It cites examples from works including the Analects, Mencius, Guoyu and Shiji. These are lexicographic senses and examples; the entry does not establish a chronological path among them.
evidence.title: [A03769] 視 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (2014)
evidence.field: GSR 0553a 示 and GSR 0553h 視 reconstruction entries
evidence.text: The search result for the authors’ reconstruction table reports 示 shì MC zyijH, OC *s-gijʔ-s (show), and 視 shì MC dzyijH, OC *gijʔ-s (look, see), alongside another 視 reading MC dzyijX, OC *gijʔ. In this system the 示 and 視 去聲 readings share the rhyme and differ by the reconstructed *s- prefix; this is compatible with a phonetic relationship, though reconstruction alone does not establish the component role. The PDF could not be opened in this session, so the table transcription is treated as search-result evidence, not as an inspected page.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Local primary reading rows supplied in input packet
evidence.text: Local rows give Baxter–Sagart 2014 MC dzyijX, OC *gijʔ and MC dzyijH, OC *gijʔ-s for 視. No 示 row was supplied. This is local table data, not independently verified external evidence; the online PDF search result separately reports 示 and 視 values in the same system.

evidence.text: Unihan defines properties for simplified and traditional variants, and says these data can document cases where sources disagree. The inspected standard page explains the properties but does not give the specific 視/视 row.

evidence.text: The file page identifies 視-oracle.svg as a modern Inkscape vector depiction of an oracle-script-style graph, says it is based on the J20963 image on hanziyuan.net and lists other reference databases, and offers the representation under a public-domain release. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph or scan of an ancient artifact. The page history records a 2016 version with components 目 and 示; the current version is described as a clearer form sourced from 見 at Richard Sears, so the source page itself signals interpretive variation.
evidence.title: File:視-oracle.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: 字形演变 labels; 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The page reproduces the received Shuowen gloss 瞻也。从見、示 and Duan Yucai’s explicit 从見。示聲. Its form catalogue labels images with inscriptions and periods, including early and middle Western Zhou bronzes, Chu slips, Qin slips and Western Han clerical writing. The page is a transcription/catalogue; labels alone do not independently date every item or establish a complete graphic lineage.
evidence.title: 「視」字的说文解字

gaps: The image file is a modern redraw of an oracle-style glyph, not an ancient artifact image. Its original file URL was obtained from the exact Commons page, but the web tool could not open the upload host because of a cache miss.

A specific official Unicode record establishing 視→视 as the standardized simplified counterpart was not retrievable. The dossier and general dictionary sources identify the relationship, but classification as simplified_form lacks independently inspected official character-specific confirmation in this run.

The Baxter–Sagart source PDF search result supplied readings for both 示 and 視 in one system, but opening the PDF failed; the specific 示 reading comparison is therefore less securely inspected than the graphic evidence and Duan Yucai’s explicit phonetic analysis.

The first securely interpretable evidence discussed in the inspected scholarly article is Shang oracle-bone material, but no absolute date was assigned to an individual token. Western Zhou bronze examples and Guodian Chu slips are discussed; the latter are broadly Warring States period.
Although the MOE dictionary lists senses and classical citations, chronology and derivational links among senses such as observe, treat as, care for, administer and compare remain unestablished here.

The early pictograph’s person-and-eye interpretation and its distinction from 見 are scholarly readings supported by contextual distribution and Chu manuscript contrasts; individual archaic graphs can remain disputed. An earlier interpretation as 望 is explicitly reported and rejected by 裘錫圭.

items.period: Shang oracle script style; modern digital depiction based on a cited J20963 database image
items.caption: A modern redraw of an oracle-style graph identified as 視; paleographic analysis distinguishes this standing-person form from the seated-person graph read as 見.
items.alt: Black line drawing of an archaic graph with an eye above a standing human figure.
items.selection_reason: Shows the early graphic contrast discussed by 裘錫圭; the file page documents its modern redraw status and provenance.
items.rights: Public-domain release stated on the Wikimedia Commons file page.

limitations.text: This is an interpretive modern vector redraw, not a photograph or direct facsimile of an excavated oracle bone. The Commons page lists conflicting/consequential source details in its history, so use it to illustrate a proposed graph form rather than as standalone paleographic proof.
